review_comment: Should this reference the `UPGRADED_TO_VERSION` in `SystemIndices`, or are they intentionally kept separate?
This field is actually not used - I'll remove it in the next PR
Good question. To be honest, I do not know, but it is used in plugins everywhere this way. I'll ask about this in our channel.

Can you help me understand when this codepath is executed?  I'm a bit unsure of the context that motivates the changes in this function.  Why do we now differentiate if `indexMigrationInProgress`, and then update the mappings/settings/indexName differently for each branch of execution?

The other branch is executed when the request comes from an external system (e.g. Kibana), where we ignore settings/mappings/aliases/index name from the request, instead taking them from the index descriptor. Here, when the request is part of a system index migration, it includes settings and mappings specifically created by `SystemIndexMigrator` for that process, so we use them. (I doubt there's any difference in real world, but some tests rely on this behavior). Additionally, we don't create an alias in this case because it already exists, pointing to the current index, and SystemIndexMigrator will handle it later. Finally, regarding the index name – an index with `descriptor.getPrimaryIndex()` already exists, and we need to create a new index with the name `descriptor.getPrimaryIndex() + SystemIndices.UPGRADED_INDEX_SUFFIX` and this is the name from the request.

We didn't need this logic before, because we were bypassing it using MetadataCreateIndexService directly, but it is not available from plugins without introducing another transport message, which is probably too much for now

Will this will still work when _creating_ a new managed/unmanged system index?  Asking since the paths you described are:
a) migration happening for managed system index
b) migration happening for externally managed system index
Will a request for a brand new system index (or a move to a system index) hit the same logic?

No reason to to think it won't be (since tests are passing), but thought it best to check with you to be sure.

This branch is under the `if (indexMigrationInProgress)` check, so it shouldn’t be executed for a completely new index. The condition `boolean indexMigrationInProgress = cause.equals(SystemIndices.MIGRATE_SYSTEM_INDEX_CAUSE) && request.index().endsWith(SystemIndices.UPGRADED_INDEX_SUFFIX)` ensures that the request is part of migration. The `cause` value, as I understand it, can't be set via REST API, and the only place in the codebase where it's set to `SystemIndices.MIGRATE_SYSTEM_INDEX_CAUSE` is in `SystemIndexMigrator`. Therefore, any request hitting this logic is coming from migration process and not from the creation of a new system index.

Move of an existing index to a system index doesn't execute this code - it is just a metadata update of the index: `org.elasticsearch.cluster.metadata.SystemIndexMetadataUpgradeService`. System index mappings update also doesn't involve reindexing: `org.elasticsearch.indices.SystemIndexMappingUpdateService`

Do we need a test that also checks the other branch of the [conditional in TransportCreateIndexAction](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/123551/files#diff-1c709b45feab712cfd065029ecedb8b747866f771cde13eaaf6cb997d420f70eR191), or is that already represented elsewhere?
There are existing tests in this class covering that branch. And there are some IT tests as well (e.g. CreateSystemIndicesIT)
Nice improvement. I wonder if we should log the whole error stack trace  with a `warn.(message, error)` method?

I don't think it's necessary here - if the request fails because the index already exists from a previous migration but then gets successfully deleted and recreated, logging the full stack trace could make it seem like a bigger issue than it actually is. If there's a real problem with index creation, the stack trace will still appear as a suppressed exception in the following errors. At least, that's how it worked for me while debugging this code:)
